deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): this is Riemann's numerical reduction of a calibration of a bifilar magnetometer, following Gauss, 'Resultate aus den Beobachtungen des magnetischen Vereins im Jahre 1840', p. 14. Each observation set k = I..IV gives a linear relation 1 = a_k x + b_k y_k. Riemann treats a_k, b_k, y_k as complex numbers: y = M(X+iY), where X and Y are the horizontal field components along and across the line joining the upper ends of the suspension wires. Here x is independent of the magnetic directive force. The working hypothesis is that soft iron near the bar flips sign when the bar is turned through 180°. Then the iron-free value satisfies y0 = (y'+y'')/2 = (y'''+y^IV)/2, i.e. y'+y''-y'''-y^IV = 0.

Derivation (filled in by me):
- From y_k = (1 - a_k x)/b_k, the condition becomes (1/b'+1/b''-1/b'''-1/b^IV) = x(a'/b'+a''/b''-a'''/b'''-a^IV/b^IV), as on the previous page.
- Multiply by b' and factor a' out of the right side. This gives a'x = alpha/omega, where
  - alpha = 1 + b'/b'' - b'/b''' - b'/b^IV,
  - omega = 1 + (a''/b'')(b'/a') - (a'''/b''')(b'/a') - (a^IV/b^IV)(b'/a').

What the page shows: this page (9v; the right half is cut off) is an incomplete first draft of the table carried out fully on the next page.
- Header: rows log(b'/b) and log(ab'/(ba')) for columns I..IV; column I is normalised to 1 (log 0, angle 0).
- Logs of moduli of the normalised ratios b'/b_k and (a_k/b_k)(b'/a'), in Gauss's 9,xxx and 0,xxx log notation, with polar angles.
- Below these, logs of real and imaginary parts (7,31.. = log 0.002062; 8,31.. = log 0.020866).
- The complex values b'/b'' ≈ -0.99..., ab'/(ba') ≈ -5.81....
- alpha ≈ -1.420... and omega ≈ -4.8....
- log|a'x| = log|alpha/omega|: first written 9.4702469, with the corrected value 9.4675959 squeezed in above.
- Then log|(a_k/b_k) b' x| for k = II, III, IV, i.e. log|ab'/(ba')|_k + log|a'x|. Values: 0.2351699, 9.8125653, 9.8849391; the angles are cut off (on the next page: 184°55'46.3", 97°13'16.3", 276°57'9.3").

Where the next page goes: these feed b'y_k = b'/b_k - (a_k/b_k) b' x. The iron-free combination then gives b'y ≈ 0.7048+0.0603i, as found on the next page.

The isolated note '62°34'12.5"' on the left leaf is an angle of unknown role (possibly related to P = 151°14'52.3" from the previous page). Its connection is not determinable.
errors: The first value log|a'x| = 9.4702469 is wrong. It equals 0.1524342 - 0.6821834, using an erroneous log|omega| = 0.6821834. The correct log|omega| is 0.6848422, which gives 9.4675959. Riemann caught this and corrected it, here and on the next page.

The three values log|(a_k/b_k) b'x| on this page (0.2351699, 9.8125653, 9.8849391) were all computed with the wrong 9.4702469 rather than the corrected value. They are therefore too large by 0.0026510. Riemann later recomputed the downstream real/imaginary logs on the next page (the struck rows 9.4687694/0.2335606n replaced by 9.4661184/0.2309096n), but the lines 0.2351699 etc. were left uncorrected.

Additional slip in the III value: 0.3423784 + 9.4702469 - 10 = 9.8126253, but 9.8125653 is written. The digits appear interchanged ('62' vs '56'), a discrepancy of 6e-5 in the log. (With the corrected log|a'x| the value should be 9.8099743.)

Otherwise every check I made is consistent: log|b'/b''| = 9.9998758; its angle 180°7'5.5"; log|alpha| = 0.1524342; arg alpha = 180°14'36.2"; arg omega = 175°31'9.4"; arg(a'x) = 4°43'26.8"; the summed angles.

results.what: Elimination of the soft-iron influence by assuming it reverses with a 180° turn of the bar, giving a'x = alpha/omega from four position equations 1 = a x + b y.
results.modern_name: Linear elimination / reversal method in bifilar magnetometer calibration (Gauss's method with complex-number bookkeeping)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Resultate 1840) for the bifilar apparatus theory; reversal methods are standard experimental practice

results.what: Numerical evaluation of complex quotients via logarithms of moduli and polar angles (and logs of real/imaginary parts).
results.modern_name: Polar-form complex arithmetic with log tables

deep.surprise_reason: Routine numerical reduction of magnetometer data, probably connected with Riemann's work with Weber in Göttingen around 1853. It is mildly interesting as evidence of Riemann's experimental and computational activity and his use of complex numbers for 2D field components. Nothing mathematically new.
